question: If a solution changes the colour of blue litmus paper to red, what will the pH of this solution be?
solution:
Correct answer is __**less than 7.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• As the solution changes the colour of blue litmus paper to red, the solution is acidic in nature.
 
• So the pH of the solution will be **less than 7.**
 
• pHs less than 7 are **acidic** while pHs greater than 7 are alkaline (basic).
 
• pH is **a measure of how acidic/basic water is.**
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/99f49a572b0e7b3848ac4d73b9551d953e6a316b54f9e08499e4ce170b4b3e18.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​The range goes from** 0 - 14, with 7 being neutral**. 
 
• pHs of less than **7 indicate acidity**, whereas a pH of **greater than 7 indicates a base.**
 
• pH is really a measure of the relative amount of free** hydrogen and hydroxyl ions in the water.**
